text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
He went through all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.'
Every valley shall be filled in, every mountain and hill made low; the crooked ways shall become straight, and the rough roads smooth.
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God."
So he said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Produce fruit worthy of repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you, God is able to raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.
The axe is already laid at the root of the trees; every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "What then should we do?"
He answered them, "Whoever has two tunics should share with the one who has none, and whoever has food should do the same."

versions.text: He answered them, "Whoever has two shirts should share with the one who has none, and whoever has food should do the same."
versions.explanation: χιτών refers to the inner garment or tunic; "tunics" is more accurate to the ancient garment than the modern-sounding "shirts," while still reading smoothly.

text: Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
He told them, "Collect no more than the amount appointed to you."

versions.text: He told them, "Collect no more than you are authorized to."
versions.explanation: The sentence ends with a dangling preposition ("authorized to"), which stumbles when read aloud. Rephrasing keeps the sense of τὸ διατεταγμένον (what has been ordered/appointed) and gives the line a natural close.

text: Soldiers too asked him, "And what should we do?" He said to them, "Do not extort money from anyone, do not accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your wages."
The people were filled with expectation, and everyone was wondering in their hearts whether John might be the Christ.
John answered them all, "I baptize you with water. But one mightier than I is coming, and I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
And with many other exhortations he proclaimed the good news to the people.
But when Herod the tetrarch was rebuked by him about Herodias, his brother's wife, and about all the other evil things he had done,
he added this to them all: he shut John up in prison.
When all the people were being baptized, Jesus too was baptized, and as he was praying, heaven was opened
and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began his work. He was the son, as was supposed, of Joseph, the son of Heli,

versions.text: Jesus himself was about thirty years old when he began his ministry. He was the son, as was supposed, of Joseph, the son of Heli,
versions.explanation: The Greek ἀρχόμενος stands alone without an object; "his ministry" supplies a specific term not in the text. "His work" is a lighter supplement, or a footnote could note that the Greek simply reads "when he began."
